title: Dallas Fed Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey (December 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET, the year's last regional survey and the first clean 10:30 window this series has had in 2026
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,458 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher. The table headed `2026 Release Dates` carries the column headers `Survey Period` and `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)`, the publisher's caveat that 'The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT. While we strive to ensure the information is published to our website in a timely manner, we cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online', and the row `December | Tuesday, Dec. 29`. 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET. Independently corroborated from the publisher's own report archive: the November reports for 2020-2025 each print a 'Next release:' line naming that year's December release date (Dec. 29 2020, Dec. 28 2021, Dec. 28 2022, Dec. 27 2023, Dec. 31 2024, Dec. 30 2025), so the December edition has landed inside Dec 27-31 in every one of the six years the archive covers. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records and neither of which any source quality can clear: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (`FED:` is scoped to federalreserve.gov's FOMC calendar), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the single prior proposal first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-29.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28.json, now shadowed and inert. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT PROPOSAL'S PROVENANCE, both from the primary re-read today. (1) There is NO one-month reporting lag: the publisher's table is headed `Survey Period | Release`, and every row releases the SAME month's survey at that month's end (`January | Tuesday, Jan. 27` … `December | Tuesday, Dec. 29`). November alone spills to Dec. 1 because the manufacturing twin's last-Monday slot that month IS the last business day — the mechanic dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01's leg 10 already computed at 35/240 months. December data really is collected in December (field window derived Dec 15-23, matching the sourced Dec-2025 window verbatim). (2) The proposal justified the row partly on 12-29 'already carrying consumer-confidence-2026-12-29' — that slot was REFUTED three days earlier by its own research (2026-09-06): the Conference Board's December print is at consumer-confidence-2026-12-22, and no Conference Board release lands on 12-29. THE ROW STILL EARNS ITS PLACE, and for a better reason than the one proposed: removing the phantom 10:00 print makes 2026-12-29 the ONLY 2026 date on which this survey's 10:30 slot has no macro release inside 90 minutes of it — FHFA HPI and Case-Shiller sit at 9:00, the 7-Year auction at 13:00 — where 12-01 had ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS at 10:00. That is the first clean attribution window the series has had all year, and it is why this entry is worth reading rather than merely counting. Read-it-do-not-trade-it all the same: `symbols: []`, `low` impact, `estimate` date, and the clean window lands in the Dec 26-31 stretch where SPY's cash session is positive only 41.3% of the time (n=92) on 0.70x normal volume — clean is not the same as readable. 2026-12-29 is also the EXACT calendar twin of 2020-12-29 (Dec 24 Thu, Dec 25 Fri holiday, Dec 28 Mon, Dec 29 Tue, Dec 31 Thu), which was itself a sourced TSSOS December release date — the same twin the treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29 lane derived independently from Treasury's auction block on the same day.
